protected_surfaces.accepted_f1_pack: All 34 leaves beneath the accepted contract root are byte-immutable in F2.
protected_surfaces.phase0_to_phase5: Every path or prefix in the accepted contract protected-paths.txt is byte-immutable, including package metadata, existing CI/release workflows, README files, CLI, and existing governance/ingest/navigation/retrieval/watcher semantics.
protected_surfaces.contract_drift: Any accepted schema, registry, vector, limit, operation, projection, or expected-outcome change is forbidden and triggers D0-15 stop.

implementation_scope: Reference TypeScript authority engine using Node built-in SQLite with exactly 16 normalized tables.
Internal owner/admin service boundary for the accepted 1 bootstrap and 24 owner operations, plus reference capability hooks for all 7 public authenticated operations.

Identity, external mapping, credential, session, policy, activity, audit, retention, rate, replay/idempotency, generations, snapshots, cursors, opaque references, and reference effect-outbox authority state.
POSIX reference physical storage, authority lease, external anchor, bootstrap/migration, backup, restore, restore-abort, and crash recovery; Windows fails closed as platform unavailable.
Focused unit/integration/reference tests and an F2-only Linux hosted qualification workflow.
explicit_exclusions: No accepted F1 pack mutation except runtime read/import of its immutable bytes.
No protected Phase 0-5 semantic path mutation.
No F3 MCP stdio or loopback HTTP transport, tool facade, initialize/session transport, or protocol projection implementation.
No F4 independently authored adversarial expectation pack.
No F5 cross-platform, ACL, crash, or evidence closeout claim.
No irreversible Navigation Effects execution; only the accepted authority outbox/bridge state boundary.
No Lite work, README reconciliation, package export/public API claim, merge, PR, release, deployment, activation, or publication.
stop_conditions: Accepted F1 bytes are insufficient to determine an exact implementation outcome.
A required implementation path falls outside the frozen 14-path inventory.
A protected or accepted-contract byte would need to change.
A test would need a new expected outcome rather than exercising an accepted outcome.
A platform guarantee cannot be proved; the reference implementation must instead return GKOS_P6_PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE.
